findings.title: Rescheduled reminders still use immediate SendGrid cancellation
findings.body: This passes `true` for `immediateDelete`, so rescheduling still POSTs cancellations directly to SendGrid instead of marking the reminder `cancelled` and letting `scheduleEmailReminders` cancel it close to the send time. That reintroduces the pending-cancellation limit that this PR is meant to fix: after enough reschedules, SendGrid cancellations fail and the old reminders are still sent. Because this immediate path also does not set `cancelled`, a failed cancellation has no DB marker for the cron to retry. Use the deferred cancellation path for reschedules, or otherwise persist the cancellation for retry.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget
findings.body: The calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` are not awaited. For email reminders the actual cancellation work is now the async DB update that sets `cancelled`; if the serverless invocation ends before that update completes, the reminder is never marked and the cron will not cancel the SendGrid email. This is the core regression path for cancelled bookings. Collect these promises and await them before returning. The same fire-and-forget pattern also appears in the reschedule and workflow handlers.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts all reminder cancellations
findings.body: The whole cancellation loop is inside one `try/catch`, and the collected `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are only awaited after the loop. If a single `client.request` fails (invalid/already-cancelled batch, rate limit, etc.), the code jumps to `catch`, skips every remaining `remindersToCancel`, and never executes the delete promises already collected. Those reminders stay in the DB, and the same failing reminder can block every subsequent cron run, so cancelled emails are still sent. Handle each reminder independently and delete/flag it per reminder.

findings.title: Immediate cancellation does not delete or mark the WorkflowReminder row
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, the function returns after the SendGrid request without deleting the row or setting `cancelled`. In the reschedule path this leaves the old booking's reminder with `scheduled: true` and the old `referenceId` until the cron's past-date cleanup. It also means a failed SendGrid call is invisible to the cron retry mechanism. The immediate path should delete the row or set a persisted state so failed cancellations can be retried.

findings.title: No index supports the new cron cancellation query
findings.body: The cron now repeatedly queries `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled = true` and a `scheduledDate` range, but the migration only adds the column. On a large `WorkflowReminder` table this is a full scan every 15 minutes. Add an index, preferably a partial index for cancelled reminders, or document why it is intentionally omitted.
